ai_summary:
Scottish wind output is currently estimated at 1.7 GW, operating at 16.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity, within a total GB wind output of 8.3 GW. Scotland’s renewable fleet delivers a Scottish carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, contrasting sharply with the GB-wide carbon intensity of 165 gCO2/kWh and illustrating the persistent infrastructure constraints dividing regional electricity networks.

Because cross-border transmission corridors cannot accommodate all northern renewable generation, Scottish generation curtailed so far today stands at 578 MWh via Balancing Mechanism turn-down instructions. This curtailment has already accrued a direct constraint cost of about £38,660 so far today. Substituting this clean energy required an estimated 109,820 m3 of gas burned elsewhere across the grid, releasing an avoidable 202 tonnes of CO2.

Annualising today's run rate produces an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £14 million. When recovered across national electricity demand through system balancing charges, this constraint adds an estimated £0.05/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK. These metrics demonstrate that overcoming transmission export bottlenecks is vital to prevent wasteful thermal re-dispatch, protect consumer bills from avoidable network surcharges, and fully harness Scotland's zero-carbon potential.
